# Song of Solomon Chapter 7 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**7:1** How-beautiful [mah yofu] are-your-feet [fe'amayikh] in-sandals [ba-ne'alim], daughter [bat] of-a-noble [nadiv]. The-curves [chammuqei] of-your-thighs [yerekayikh] [are] like-ornaments [kemo chala'im], the-work [ma'aseh] of-the-hands [yedei] of-a-craftsman [amman].

**7:2** Your-navel [sharrekh] [is a] round [aggan] bowl [ha-sahar]; let-it-not-lack [al yechsar] mixed-wine [ha-mazeg]. Your-belly [bitnekh] [is a] heap [aremat] of-wheat [chittim], hedged [sugah] with-lilies [ba-shoshannim].

**7:3** Your-two [shenei] breasts [shadayikh] [are] like-two [ki-shnei] fawns [oferim], twins [te'omei] of-a-gazelle [tzeviyah].

**7:4** Your-neck [tzavvarekh] [is] like-a-tower [ke-migdal] of-ivory [ha-shen]; your-eyes [einayikh] [are] pools [berekhot] in-Heshbon [be-Cheshbon] by-the-gate [al sha'ar] of-Bath-Rabbim [Bat Rabbim]. Your-nose [appekh] [is] like-the-tower [ke-migdal] of-Lebanon [ha-Levanon], watching [tzofeh] toward [penei] Damascus [Dammaseq].

**7:5** Your-head [roshekh] upon-you [alayikh] [is] like-Carmel [ka-Karmel], and-the-hair [ve-dallat] of-your-head [roshekh] [is] like-purple [ka-argaman]; a-king [melekh] [is] bound [asur] in-the-tresses [ba-rehatim].

**7:6** How-beautiful [mah yofit] and-how-pleasant [u-mah na'amt], O-love [ahavah], among-delights [ba-ta'anugot]!

**7:7** This your-stature [qomatekh] is-like [damtah] a-palm-tree [le-tamar], and-your-breasts [ve-shadayikh] like-clusters [le-ashkelot].

**7:8** I-said [amarti]: "I-will-climb [e'eleh] the-palm-tree [be-tamar], I-will-seize [ochazah] its-branches [be-sansinav]." And-let [ve-na] your-breasts [shadayikh] be [yihyu] like-clusters [ke-eshkelot] of-the-vine [ha-gefen], and-the-scent [ve-re'ach] of-your-nose [appekh] like-apples [ka-tappuchim].

**7:9** And-your-palate [ve-chikkekh] like-good [ke-yein ha-tov] wine — going [holekh] to-my-beloved [le-dodi] smoothly [le-meisharim], flowing [dovev] over-the-lips [siftei] of-sleepers [yeshenim].

**7:10** I [ani] [am] my-beloved's [le-dodi], and-upon-me [ve-alai] [is] his-desire [teshuqato].

**7:11** Come [lekhah], my-beloved [dodi], let-us-go-out [netze] to-the-field [ha-sadeh]; let-us-lodge [nalinah] among-the-henna [ba-kefarim].

**7:12** Let-us-rise-early [nashkimah] to-the-vineyards [la-keramim]; let-us-see [nir'eh] if the-vine [ha-gefen] has-budded [parchah], [if] the-blossom [ha-semadar] has-opened [pittach], [if] the-pomegranates [ha-rimmonim] have-bloomed [henetzu]; there [sham] I-will-give [etten] my-loves [et dodai] to-you [lakh].

**7:13** The-mandrakes [ha-duda'im] give [natenu] fragrance [re'ach], and-over our-doors [ve-al petacheinu] [are] all [kol] choice-fruits [megadim], new [chadashim] and-also [gam] old [yeshanim]; my-beloved [dodi], I-have-stored-them [tzafanti] for-you [lakh].

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — The ascending wasf:** Unlike the descending *wasf* of chapter 4 (head to breasts), this *wasf* ascends from feet to head. The reversal may reflect the different vantage point — the woman is being observed as she dances (cf. 6:13).

**v.5 — "a king bound in the tresses":** The Hebrew *melekh asur ba-rehatim* is striking — the king (or: a king) is captivated, imprisoned by her hair. Love as captivity is a recurring theme.

**v.10 — "his desire is for me":** The word *teshuqah* (desire/longing) appears only three times in the Hebrew Bible: Genesis 3:16 (the woman's desire for her husband), Genesis 4:7 (sin's desire for Cain), and here. In Genesis 3:16, the power dynamic is asymmetric; here it is reciprocal and positive.

*-- EMET*
